audit.why: Packet win rate is 54.67% over 225 games — Zac-favoured. No elo-tier language appears anywhere in the entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content level chart gives Sion 4 of 7 stages and Zac zero, while Zac wins 54.67%. The full layer disagrees with its own content layer: phases[] read Skill/Zac/Zac/Skill/Skill/Zac/Zac.
audit.why: Two layers of the same matchup contradict each other, and the one shown as the level chart contradicts the win rate.
audit.corrected: Aligned both layers to Skill/Zac/Zac/Skill/Skill/Zac/Sion — Zac-favoured through the middle, Sion keeping the late-teamfight stage that the existing prose already argues for.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Sion permanently stacks maximum health with Soul Furnace (W) while Zac's Unstable Matter (W) deals a percentage of the target's maximum health.
audit.why: This is the mechanical reason Zac beats Sion: every point of max HP Sion banks makes Zac's 5-second-cooldown W hit him harder. It also directly refutes the "resistances-invalidated / raw armour is wrong" note in _missing-interactions.json, which points at the wrong side of the trade.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[5] and the first-item stage: Sion's stacked HP is what makes Zac's W scale.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (W Soul Furnace: "When Sion kills enemies, he passively gains maximum Health")

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer (E) is never mentioned, and the entry repeatedly tells Zac to farm safely without noting what Sion does to a minion line.
audit.why: Riot's own text: if the shockwave hits a minion or monster it is knocked back, damaging, slowing and shredding armour of everything it passes through. Standing behind your own wave against Sion is worse than standing beside it — the opposite of the default advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says Sion's R "is a strong engage but it's predictable, and you can body-block or side-step it" without saying what does NOT stop it.
audit.why: Zac's only two commit tools (Stretching Strikes, Elastic Slingshot) are displacement. A Zac player reading "you can stop it" will try to knock Sion out of the charge and lose the fight. Body-blocking works because a champion collision ends the charge; a knock-up does not.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1].text to name the distinction explicitly and add the rank-1 cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sion.json (R: "When he collides with an enemy he deals damage and knocks them up")

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death (P) is called "undying passive" with no mechanical content.
audit.why: Sion's reanimated attacks deal bonus damage based on the target's MAXIMUM health and heal him. Against a Heartsteel Zac that is the single worst body to stand next to after Sion dies — and it is why killing Sion first in a teamfight is not the clean win it looks like.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says "Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Track it before every engage" with no numbers, and the window after Unstoppable Onslaught is never quantified.
audit.why: The brief says the real numbers beat vague advice. Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 and Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s at rank 1 — a two-minute window that decides when Zac can take an objective fight.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns with the rank-1 figures for both Sion spells and Zac's own Elastic Slingshot.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says "Sion's Q wind-up and shield out-trade Zac" at level 1.
audit.why: Sion has one ability at level 1. He cannot have both Decimating Smash and Soul Furnace, so the stated level-1 threat cannot happen.

edits.before: Level 1 Sion's Q wind-up and shield out-trade Zac.
edits.after: Level 1 Sion has one spell; the Q wind-up tells.

edits.before: At 2 his charged knock-up punishes any Zac commit.
edits.after: At 2 Zac's W %HP chip out-paces Sion's 10s Q cycle.

edits.before: Level 3 Sion still wins trades through shield sustain.
edits.after: Level 3 Zac's E engage opens on Sion's slow Q wind-up.

edits.before: First item stays even; neither out-damages the other.
edits.after: First item, Sion's stacked HP makes Zac's W hurt.

edits.before: Late, Sion's R-Q CC chain and undying passive out-scale Zac.
edits.after: Late, Sion's R-Q chain and his max-HP-scaling revive win.

edits.before: Sion's Q (Decimating Smash) charged knock-up plus his shield W punish your early aggression — if you E in and eat a fully-charged Q you get stunned and traded down, so respect the wind-up levels 1-3.
edits.after: Sion's Decimating Smash (Q) is a 10s wind-up at rank 1 — dodge it and he has nothing to trade with. Don't hide behind your own minions either: his Roar of the Slayer (E) knocks one back through you and shreds armour.

edits.before: Around 6 it evens out — Sion's Unstoppable Onslaught (R) is a strong engage but it's predictable, and you can body-block or side-step it and answer with your own E-R engage.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught (R) is 140s at rank 1. Your Q and E knock-ups will not stop the charge — only a champion body will, so block it or side-step, then answer with your own E-R.

edits.before: Sion out-scales into full teamfights — his R charge and Q knock-up chain more reliable CC than your single engage, and his passive undying lets him keep fighting after you blow cooldowns.
edits.after: Sion out-scales in full teamfights — his R-into-Q chain lands more CC than your single engage, and Glory in Death (P) makes his post-death attacks scale off max health, so your bar is the one it wants.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 favour Sion: his charged Q knock-up and shield W let him win any trade where you commit E, so don't slingshot into a wind-up — farm and only punish after he whiffs the Q.
edits.after: Level 1 is Sion's — respect the charged Q. From 2 your W chips a percentage of his health pool and blobs pay for it, and his 10s Q is the only thing punishing you, so trade the moment it is spent.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sion carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Sion's R-Q chain out-CCs your single engage in a 5v5. Carry threat 7/10 — take the game on the side lane before he groups.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — charged = knockup, 10s at rank 1. Dodge it, then commit. - Unstoppable Onslaught: 140s at rank 1 — a huge window once spent. - Your E: 21s at rank 1, never spend it on chip.

notes: Chart-side fields (win[N], phases[N].side) are enum-valued — "Sion"/"Zac"/"Skill" cannot be swapped inside a +/-10% length band, so those five edits will fail a literal length check. They are the flagged defect and cannot be expressed any other way; apply them exempt from the band or reject them knowingly. NOT PROPAGATED: _missing-interactions.json tells this matchup that "Sion bypasses stacking resistances (Glory in Death (P), Soul Furnace (W)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here." Soul Furnace is a shield plus permanent max-HP growth; it does not bypass resistances. The real interaction runs the other way (Sion's HP feeds Zac's %max-HP W) and that is what I wrote instead.
